## <strong>Working Papers</strong>
1. [Mental Healthcare Facilities and Mortality: Evidence from Local Access and Insurance Expansion](Ola-Yusuff-Mental-Healthcare-Facilities-Mortality.pdf) | [SSRN](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7087058)<br>
*Status: Under review*

<details>
<summary>Abstract (click to expand)</summary>
<div style="margin-top: 10px; text-align: justify;">

Do mental health treatment facilities save lives? Using county-level variation in facility openings from County Business Patterns data matched to the universe of U.S. mortality records (1999-2016), I estimate heterogeneity-robust event studies of a county's first facility: all-cause deaths fall by roughly 3 percent, about 1 percent of deaths in population-weighted per-person terms, with no differential pre-trends. In the full county panel, each additional facility prevents 1.56 deaths per 100,000 residents annually. A cause-of-death decomposition attributes the effect to mental health related deaths and to chronic-disease deaths, with placebo causes unchanged, direct evidence that treatment spills over onto physical health. Medicaid expansion amplifies facility effects, indicating that insurance coverage and treatment infrastructure are complements: facilities in high-uninsurance expansion counties prevent 1.80 all-cause and 0.16 MBD deaths per 100,000. Facilities operate partly by connecting patients to disability benefits and prescription treatment. Conservative estimates imply $11.7 million in annual net benefits per facility.

</div>
</details>
